title: Jukebox Jenny and the made-up social security numbers
summary: Barnet wrote the song Fifty Million Nickels for the film and invented twenty social security numbers to collect the band's checks before leaving town.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: That'd be fun. Every once in a while some really great music shows up in cartoons. It's a nice shock. The next one, "Jukebox Jenny," 1942. 61 minutes, directed by Harold Young. Formula romance with music about a record salesman who builds jukebox star out of a young singer. Features Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra, with Cliff Leeman, drums, Wingy Manone and His Orchestra, the Milt Herb Trio and the Kingsmen, plus the song, "Fifty Million Nickels," by Charlie Barnet.
Yeah. I guess you could call that one of my tunes with lyrics.
You wrote both the music and the lyrics, huh?

Yeah, and it was a pretty horrible song, but it -- I don't even remember it, the melody or anything about it, but that was the picture, Ken Murray was in that, and Harriet Hilliard, that's Harriet Nelson now. Well, she was then. But they played the leads. I'll tell you something funny about that picture. We did it and we were leaving for New York, and I said, "We've got to get the money." We were leaving like that night, and at that time the withholding had just come in, as far as bands were concerned, and they said, "Well, we've got to have the social security numbers, or we can't give you the checks." Well, the band is already gone. I said, "Okay," and I made up like 20 social security numbers out of my head and gave them to Universal and I got the checks, which of course a week or so later we supplied them with the real numbers, but they were bound they weren't going to release those checks without the social security numbers.
That's the thing about a musician, he can always improvise on his feet, right?
The only one that was correct was mine.
